questions.prompt: Where is it unlawful in Abbeville to sell, buy, or possess an open container of alcohol?
choices: On any public street, sidewalk, parking area, playground, or park
questions.answer: On any public street, sidewalk, parking area, playground, or park
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Giving prisoner alcoholic beverage, § 12-3(1); prohibited acts by taxicab drivers, § 20-39(a). State Law reference— Alcohol and alcoholic beverages, S.C. Code 1976, Title 61.

All the provisions and requirements of state law governing alcoholic beverages, insofar
               as those provisions can have application within the city, are hereby adopted and made
               a part of this chapter as fully as though set out in this section. All persons within
               the city shall strictly comply with all the regulations imposed by such provisions,
               when applicable. (Code 1979, § 7-3-1)

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to sell or buy any alcoholic beverage, or have
               in his possession any open container of alcoholic beverage, on any public street,
               sidewalk, parking area, playground, or park. (b) It shall be unlawful for any person while a passenger, occupant or driver of any motor
               vehicle to drink or have in possession any open container of alcoholic liquor or beer
               or wine on any street, highway, park or other public place. (c) Alcohol at events. (1) Within the boundaries of Downtown Abbeville, a temporary event permit for a public
               or private event may be granted by the approval of city council that includes the
               consumption and possession of beer and/or wine within the defined area of the Historic
               Overlay District. This permit may be for a public or private event and includes all
               streets, highways, parks, and/or public places within the designated event area. Private events shall be approved via the standard event approval process and public
               events shall be approved via the annual road closure request approved by city council. (2) The permit required by this subsection shall be issued on a form deemed suitable by
               the city manager. Conditions of…

questions.prompt: If an unpaved Abbeville County road is not listed on the official speed schedule, what is the speed limit?
questions.answer: 20 miles per hour
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Powers of local authorities, S.C. Code 1976, § 56-5-710; notice of certain local regulation
               required, S.C. Code 1976, § 56-5-720; local traffic control devices, S.C. Code 1976,
               § 56-5-940.

It shall be unlawful for a person to drive a motor vehicle on any road maintained
               by the county in excess of the speed limit for such road as established from time
               to time, on a schedule and available for public inspection in the town administrative
               offices. If a speed limit is not provided on Schedule A for any road maintained by
               the county, then it shall be unlawful for a person to drive a motor vehicle on such
               road in excess of the following speed limits: (1) Unpaved roads . All unpaved roads maintained by the county shall have a speed limit of 20 miles
                  per hour. (2) Paved dead-end roads . All paved roads maintained by the county that dead-end (roads that do not connect
                  to two other roads at each end) shall have a speed limit of 25 miles per hour. (3) Paved through roads . All paved roads maintained by the county that connect to two other roads at each
                  end shall have a speed limit of 40 miles per hour. (Ord. No. 2013-08, § 1, 9-9-2013)

A person violating the speed limits established by this article is guilty of a misdemeanor
               and, upon conviction for a first offense, must be fined or imprisoned as follows: (1) In excess of the posted limit but not in excess of ten miles an hour, by a fine of
                  not less than $15.00 nor more than $25.00; (2) In excess of ten miles an hour but less than 15 miles an hour above the posted limit,
                  by a fine of not less than $25.00 not more than $50.00; (3) In excess of 15 miles an hour but less than 25 miles an hour above the posted limit,
                  by a fine of not less than $50.00 nor more…

questions.prompt: In Aiken, which of these is not treated as “alcoholic liquors”?
choices: Lager or rice beer used as a drink
Wine made only for home use and not sold
Any mix that contains alcohol and is used as a beverage
questions.answer: Wine made only for home use and not sold
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Businesses, ch. 12; alcoholic beverages prohibited at garage sales, § 34-39. State Law reference— Alcoholic beverages, S.C. Code 1976, title 61.

For the purpose of this chapter, the words "alcoholic liquors" shall be construed
               to mean any spirituous, malt, vinous, fermented, brewed (whether lager or rice beer)
               or other liquors, or any compound or mixture thereof, by whatever name known, which
               contains alcohol and is used as a beverage. This definition shall not extend to and
               include wine, when made for home consumption and which is not sold by the maker thereof
               or any other person, nor shall it apply to any beverage heretofore or hereafter declared
               by the statutory law of the state to be nonalcoholic or nonintoxicating. (Code 1980, § 4-1) Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2 . State Law reference— Similar provisions, S.C. Code 1976, § 61-6-20.

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person either to manufacture, store, receive, have in
               possession, transport, buy, sell, barter, exchange or deliver any alcoholic liquors
               in the corporate limits of the city, except as permitted by state law. (b) It shall be unlawful for any person to have in his possession, or to purchase or otherwise
               procure, within the corporate limits of the city, any alcoholic liquors, other than
               such as shall have been purchased from a dealer duly licensed by the state, or which
               does not have affixed thereto revenue stamps required under the laws of the state. (Code 1980, § 4-2)

It shall be unlawful for any person within the corporate limits of the city to: (1) Publicly engage in the drinking of alcoholic liquors. (2) Publicly engage in the drinking of alcoholic liquors in the presence of a passenger

Appeals from decisions of town officials made in enforcing this chapter shall be made
               to the town council. (Code 2003, § 16.222)

It is unlawful to camp on any public property, including streets, without permission
               from the mayor. (Code 2003, § 16.221)

It is unlawful for the owner of lands or lots of lands within the corporate limits
               to fail to keep in good repair the fences on same, which are adjacent to any street
               or alley. All dilapidated fences adjacent to streets or alleys are declared a nuisance
               and may be removed by the town. (Code 2003, § 16.220)

               on public property within the corporate limits. Application for permit to distribute
               advertising matter shall be made to the clerk-treasurer. The fee for such permits
               shall be in the amount provided in the town fee schedule. (Code 2003, § 15.202)

               property within the corporate limits, without prior approval of the clerk-treasurer,

questions.prompt: What language must Barnwell County use to conduct its regular business?
questions.answer: English
questions.excerpt:
(a) English is the official language of the county, and all business shall be conducted
               in English. Another language may be used in emergency situations or as required by
               state and federal law to protect the health and civil liberties of individuals. (b) The county shall not employ any persons who are unable to document that they are legal
               residents of the United States of America. Also, county vendors shall certify that,
               to the extent feasible, they do not employ illegal immigrants. (c) County law enforcement shall make a reasonable effort to determine the citizenship
               or residency status of all persons booked into the county detention center. (d) Agencies that receive county funding (including council contingency funds) may not
               knowingly employ or serve illegal immigrants except as required by state or federal
               law. The agencies must make a reasonable attempt to determine the immigration status
               of apparent immigrants. ( Ord. No. 2007-231 , 11-6-2007)

Any person who distributes or sells any substance under the pretense that the substance
               is an illegal drug, illegal narcotic, or controlled substance when the substance is,
               in fact, not an illegal drug, illegal narcotic or controlled substance shall be guilty
               of the sale of counterfeit drugs for the purpose of this section and, upon conviction,
               shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor. ( Ord. No. 2005-202 , § 1, 4-5-2005)

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Ambient noise means the generally prevailing sound or combination of sounds at the location where
               a listener receives the sound of the noise about which a complaint is being made.

Pursuant to the authority provided by S.C. Code 1976, § 4-9-170, the county council,
               in its capacity as the governing body of the county, hereby creates a commission to
               be known as the Spiers Landing Commission. (Code 1985, § 12-31)

The Spiers Landing commission shall be composed of nine members. Each councilmember
               shall have the authority to nominate one individual from his respective district.
               One at-large member, to be selected by the county supervisor, shall also be nominated.
               All members of the commission shall be nominated for approval and appointment by majority
               vote of the county council. (Code 1985, § 12-32)

The members of the Spiers Landing commission shall serve terms concurrent with the
               member of the council nominating them for membership. (Code 1985, § 12-34)

Members of the Spiers Landing commission shall receive no compensation for the service
               on the commission. (Code 1985, § 12-35)

The commissioners shall elect a chairperson of the Spiers Landing commission from
               among the appointed commissioners. (Code 1985, § 12-33)

The members of the Spiers Landing commission shall be responsible for advising the
               county council as to the management and operation of Spiers Landing. Commission members
               shall have no fiscal responsibility and shall not accept any funds, assets or other

questions.prompt: Can residents drink or cook with water from the town lakes?
choices: No, that use is strictly prohibited
Yes, if you have a town permit
questions.answer: No, that use is strictly prohibited
questions.excerpt:
The following are regulations affecting public lakes for use of residents and their
               guest of the town for recreation, peaceful relaxation and quiet enjoyment and to protect
               the water quality along with the animal and plant habitat in addressing the environmental
               concerns: (1) The use of lake water for drinking or cooking is strictly prohibited. (2) No swimming or diving is allowed. (3) Those who engage in boating do so at their own risk, assuming all liability for all
                  such activity. (4) Electric trolling motors only, all other power boats or motors are strictly forbidden. (5) All persons using the lakes must wear a federally approved flotation device at all
                  times. (6) The rules of safe boating must be followed at all times. (7) Fishing is strictly "hook and release," by hook and line. (8) No netting, hard lines, etc. (9) Wildlife in and around the lakes is not for human consumption. (10) No littering, dumping or fill is permitted in the lakes. (11) Lake usage is at your own risk. (12) Residents less than 12 years of age must be accompanied by an adult. (13) Nonresidents must have a permit that can be obtained from the town office. (14) A state fishing license is required. (Ord. No. 2006-01, 3-20-2006)

questions.excerpt:
(a) Except as authorized herein and subject to the provisions of S.C. Code 1976, § 5-27-910,
               it shall be unlawful for any person to stand on a highway or street located within
               the unincorporated areas of the county for the purposes of soliciting employment,
               business, or contributions from a pedestrian or an occupant of any vehicle. (b) A rescue squad, volunteer fire department, or other charitable or eleemosynary organization,
               as recognized by the office of the secretary of state for the state, may solicit funds
               from motorists on highways and streets located within the unincorporated areas of
               the county only with a permit issued by the county sheriff's office, and such permit
               shall be retained at the site of the solicitation. (c) The county sheriff's office shall issue a permit to organizations described herein;
               provided that the sheriff's office may, as a condition of such permit, impose such
               reasonable limits upon the solicitation as it determines are necessary to protect
               the health and safety of motorists, pedestrians, and those soliciting for an organization
               and to ensure that solicitation does not unreasonably impede the flow of traffic. (d) Applications for permits under this section shall be made in person at the county
               sheriff's office. Each permit application must state the name and address of the individual,
               group, entity, or organization, as filed in the office of the secretary of state,
               requesting the permit and provide a brief explanation for the purposes for, and the
               location and date of, the proposed solicitation. A separate permit application is
               required for each proposed location. Additionally, the applicant shall designate a
               responsible person, who must be present at each proposed location, on the…

               in any lake, stream, swimming pool or fountain in any such park. (Code 1983, § 12.104)

(a) No owners shall fail to provide domesticated or constrained animals or pets with proper
               shelter, sustenance or veterinary care when needed to prevent suffering. (b) When a pet or animal is found in a condition which evidences a first-time violation
               of any paragraph of section 6-1 of this chapter, the environmental services officer (ESO) shall issue a "notice of
               violation" to its owner, if known. The owner shall then have 24 hours to correct the
               violation. (c) If this violation occurs a second or subsequent time, or if the owner does not correct
               or remedy the first-time violation within twenty-four hours, or if the person violates
               any other section of this chapter, the ESO shall issue a "summons" to such person
               and the matter shall be heard before a court of competent jurisdiction. However, nothing
               in this chapter shall limit an ESO from taking immediate action, when it is deemed
               to be in the best interest of the pet or animal. (d) No person shall sell, trade, or give away as a pet any carnivorous animal that is

               listed in section 6-16 ,…

(a) The provisions of the Richland County animal control ordinance as adopted in Richand
               County Ordinance No. 019-17HR, adopting as amended chapter 5 , sections 5-1 through 5-19 of the Richland County Code of Ordinances, including all licensing requirements,
               fees and penalties set forth therein, are adopted and incorporated here by reference
               and shall apply in full force and hereafter govern the control of animals in the city.
               References in the ordinance to unincorporated areas of the county shall be interpreted
               to apply to incorporated areas of the city. A copy of the ordinance shall be kept
               on file in the office of the city clerk. Nothing in this section shall be construed
               to mean that any city ordinance or provision thereof is repealed by implication. (b) Subsequent amendments by Richland County to the county animal control provisions adopted
               in this section shall not be deemed to amend such provisions as the same apply in
               the city, and such provisions shall instead continue to apply in the city in the form
               adopted by this section until amended by city council. (c) Richland County, through any appropriate agency, department, or designee thereof,

Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Regulatory authority of city inside and outside city limits with respect to parks,
               S.C. Code 1976, § 51-15-20.

(a) Regulations. The city shall, in connection with its duties imposed by law, diligently enforce
               the provisions of this article and may adopt and issue regulations in connection therewith. (b) Expulsion. The city shall have the authority to eject from any public mall, park or other public
               property any person acting in violation of this article or the regulations adopted
               thereunder. (c) Seizure of property. The city shall have the authority to seize and confiscate any property, thing or
               device in any public mall, park or other public property used in violation of this
               article or the regulations adopted thereunder. (Code 1985, § 3-1-10; Code 1997, § 26-31)

No person in or on a public mall, park or other public property, without consent of
               the city, shall dig or remove any soil, sand, rock, stones, shrubs or plants, down
               timber or other wood materials, or make any excavation by tool, equipment, blasting
               or other means or agency. (Code 1985, § 3-1-1(1)a; Code 1997, § 26-32)

No person in or on a public mall, park or other public property, without consent of
               the city, shall construct or erect any building or structure of whatever kind, whether
               permanent or temporary in character, or run or string any public service utility into,
               upon or across such lands. (Code 1985, § 3-1-1(1)b; Code 1997, § 26-33)

questions.prompt: Which vehicles are left out of Greenwood County's annual road user fee?
questions.answer: Licensed and registered mobile homes
questions.excerpt:
(a) Annual payment. The owners of every motorized vehicle, except duly licensed and registered mobile
               homes, required to be registered and licensed in the county by the state department
               of highways and public transportation, shall pay annually to the county a county road
               user fee in such amount as may be set by the county council. (b) Collection. The road user fee shall be collected at the time as ad valorem taxes on motorized
               vehicles. (c) Use. The proceeds from the collection of such fees shall be deposited in a fund to be administered
               by the county manager, which fund shall be separate and distinct from the county general
               fund and shall be maintained in a separate bank account. The proceeds of such fund,
               together with any investment income earned thereon, must be used solely and exclusively
               for the construction, improvement, and maintenance of county roads and related drainage.
               Funds not used in any fiscal year shall be carried forward and used exclusively for
               the construction, improvement, and maintenance of county roads and related drainage. (Ord. No. 20-92, §§ I—III, 11-3-92) Editor's note— Ord. No. 20-92, §§ I—III, adopted Nov. 3, 1992, did not specifically amend the Code;
               hence, inclusion of said provisions as § 10-1-1 was at the discretion of the editor.

               The absence of a history note indicates that the provision remains unchanged from
               the original ordinance. Obvious misspellings and punctuation errors have been corrected

               and the same system of capitalization, citation to state statutes, and expression

questions.prompt: In Irmo, it is against the rules to sell liquor, beer, ale, porter, wine, or similar malt or fermented drinks to anyone under what age?
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Businesses, ch. 10; unlawful to drink in public, § 22-141. State Law reference— Alcohol and alcoholic beverages generally, S.C. Code 1976, Title 61.

All the provisions of state law contained in S.C. Code 1976, § 61-6-10 et seq., relating
               to alcoholic liquors and beverages, insofar as such provisions and amendments have
               application within the town, are hereby adopted and made a part of this chapter as
               fully and completely as though set out in this section verbatim. It shall be unlawful
               for any person to fail or refuse to comply with such provisions of state law within
               the town. (Code 1985, § 14-303)

It shall be unlawful for any person to sell liquor, beer, ale, porter, wine or any
               other similar malt or fermented beverage to a person under the age of 21 years. (Code 1985, § 14-302) State Law reference— Similar provisions, S.C. Code 1976, § 61-4-50.

It shall be unlawful for any person to purchase beer or wine while on licensed premises
               and to give beer or wine to a person to whom beer or wine cannot lawfully be sold

questions.prompt: Is it against the law to show up in public while intoxicated in Lancaster?
choices: Yes, it is unlawful to appear in public in an intoxicated condition.
No, only drinking from an open can is banned.
Only if you are on a sidewalk after dark.
It is allowed in any park.
questions.answer: Yes, it is unlawful to appear in public in an intoxicated condition.
questions.excerpt:
It shall be unlawful for any person to appear in public in the city in an intoxicated
               condition. (Code 1974, § 4-1; Code 1991, § 3-1) State Law reference— Similar provisions, S.C. Code 1976, § 16-17-530.

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to have in his possession any beer, wine, or distilled
               liquor in an open container, or in any container with a broken seal, in any public
               place within the corporate limits of the city, except as provided hereinbelow. (b) For the purposes of this section, the term "public place" shall be defined as: (1) Any real property owned by any federal, state, county, or municipal government or
               any agency thereof; and (2) Any real property, regardless of ownership, which is open to members of the public,
               save and except real property where drinking is allowed pursuant to a permit or license
               from the state. (c) The prohibition provided in subsection (a) of this section, regarding beer and wine,
               shall not be applicable to any areas designated by resolution or city council as a
               special events area, to include, but not be limited to, any public park, street sidewalk
               or any portion thereof, for limited durations, and designated as the site of a public
               festival or other special event. (d) The application of this section shall in no way affect the enforcement or prosecution
               of violations of section 4-1 or 24-89, or of any other city ordinance or state law. (Code 1974, § 4-3; Code 1991, § 3-2; Ord. No. O11-12, 11-22-2011)

(a) History. The Laurens County Parks, Recreation, and Tourism Commission was established in 1958
               by legislative act 737 and originally consisted of five members. Ordinance 293B (July
               1989) revised the commission, which now consists of seven members. Also see Ordinance
               571. (b) Purpose. The purpose of this commission is advisory and primarily is for the disposition of
               tourism funds designated to Laurens County. (c) Membership, appointment, and term. The commission shall be composed of seven members to be appointed by county council
               consisting of a representative cross section of Laurens County. Each council member
               shall be entitled to one appointment. An appointee of council shall be a registered
               elector residing in Laurens County and may be from the district of the council member
               making the appointment or from any other are of the county, at the sole discretion
               of the council member making such appointment. An appointee shall serve a term consisting
               of four years. The term of an appointee shall expire at midnight on December 31 st of the year of the appointing council member's term expiration. In the event a vacancy
               occurs, the council member for whom the appointee serves shall fill such vacancy for
               the unexpired term of the appointee. (Ord. No. 396, 9-13-1994; Ord. No. 571, attach. 8, 9-9-2003; Ord. No. 888 , Exh. A, 1-12-2021)

questions.prompt: Which people may still use unincorporated Pickens County parks between 10:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m.?

Anyone who already paid an entrance fee
No one; the parks are fully closed

questions.prompt: Before anyone can stay in a short-term rental for the first time in Port Royal, what has to happen?
choices: The town building official inspects it and finds it satisfactory
The owner just posts a sign
It only needs a business license
questions.answer: The town building official inspects it and finds it satisfactory
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Buildings, construction and related activities, Ch. 4; housing, Ch. 11; licenses and business regulations, Ch. 12; utilities, Ch. 21. State Law reference— Mobile homes and house trailers, S.C. Code 1976, § 31-17-30.

The town building official shall inspect all short-term rental units prior to their
               first occupancy, and thereafter as requested by the town manager (refer to sec. 13-1.2 ). No initial permit for occupancy shall be issued until an inspection has been completed
               and the unit found satisfactory in all respects. (Code 1980, § 11-1; Ord. No. 2024-7, § 1, 5-8-24)

(a) Every person, firm, partnership or corporation or other entity which operates as a
               landlord engaged in the business of leasing or renting any mobile home or any mobile
               home park containing four (4) or fewer units or any structure containing four (4)
               or fewer units and described in section 12-44, (Class 8, SIC# 6514 - Operators of
               Dwellings Other Than Apartment Buildings) other than apartment buildings, multiple
               units, multiple dwelling, or dwelling unit(s), and not otherwise required to pay a
               business license fee, is hereby required to purchase an annual business license from
               the town to engage in the business. For purposes of this ordinance, the operators
               or owners of any mobile home or any mobile home park containing four (4) or fewer
               such dwellings or units must make application and receive a business license. The
               application shall be accompanied by a fifteen dollar ($15.00) annual license for each
               rental unit located in the town. (b) The business license shall be issued if: (1) It has been or is determined that the property is not in violation of any ordinance
               of the town; and (2) The applicant furnishes a full legal description of all parcels…

questions.prompt: In Ridge Spring, where is it illegal to stand if you are trying to hitch a ride?
choices: Only in a travel lane of the street
On a street, sidewalk, or curb
Only at night on Main Street
questions.answer: On a street, sidewalk, or curb
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Uniform Act Regulating Traffic on Highways, local authority, S.C. Code 1976, § 56-5-30;
               powers of local authorities concerning traffic laws, S.C. Code 1976, § 56-5-710; local
               traffic control devices, S.C. Code 1976, § 56-5-930.

There is hereby adopted by reference and made a part hereof as if set out in full
               those provisions of state law known as the "Uniform Act Regulating Traffic on Highways"
               as contained in S.C. Code, title 56, chapter 5 (S.C. Code 1976, § 56-5-10 et seq.). (Code 1980, § 8-1-1)

No vehicle shall be operated within the town limits other than by a properly licensed
               driver. (Code 1980, § 8-1-2)

Drivers of all vehicles shall abide by signals of traffic officers and all automatic
               and stationary traffic signs and signals within the town limits. (Code 1980, § 8-1-3)

The chief of police, with the approval of the council, shall have authority to make,
               promulgate and enforce special traffic regulations, including the designation of one-way
               streets, dangerous intersections where traffic shall be required to slow or stop,
               school zones, safety zones and regulations as to parking, nonparking and time limits
               for parking, and to cause to be erected or placed signs, signals, markings or other
               traffic control devices for the purpose of enforcing the same. Such special regulations
               shall not become effective until the same shall have been advertised two times in
               a daily newspaper of general circulation in the town. Any person failing or refusing
               to obey any regulation so advertised shall be guilty of violation of this chapter. (Code 1980, § 8-1-4) State Law reference— Local traffic control devices must conform with state manual of standards and specifications
               for uniform systems of traffic…

questions.excerpt:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning. Alcoholic liquor means any spirituous malt, vinous, fermented, brewed or other liquor or any compound
               or mixture thereof by whatever name called or known which contains alcohol and used
               as a beverage except any beverage declared to be nonalcoholic or nonintoxicating by
               state law. Nonalcoholic and nonintoxicating beverage means all beers, ales, porter and other similar malt or fermented beverages containing
               not in excess of five percent of alcohol by weight and all wines containing not in
               excess of 21 percent of alcohol by volume are declared to be nonalcoholic and nonintoxicating
               beverages. Unlawful drug means any narcotic drugs, barbiturates, paraldehyde's, herbs, cocaine, eucaine, morphine,

questions.prompt: Can you fish in the waters of Swan Lake Gardens in Sumter?
choices: Yes, if you have a state fishing license
Yes, but only with hook and line
No. Fishing is not allowed there in any way
Only children under 12 may fish there
questions.answer: No. Fishing is not allowed there in any way
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Authority to regulate public parks, S.C. Code 1976, § 51-15-20.

It shall be unlawful for any person to fish in any way, whether by artificial tackle
               or hook and line, in the waters of Swan Lake Gardens in the city, or to disturb, in
               any way, the wildlife in Swan Lake Gardens. (Code 1976, § 22-1; Code 1998, § 58-1)

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to enter upon the premises of any park, gardens,
               ball field, basketball court, golf course, athletic track, tennis court or any other
               recreational facility or the surrounding grounds of any such park or recreational
               facility owned, leased, occupied or used by the city or county or any department,
               board, commission or subdivision thereof during any hours that such park or recreational
               facility is closed to the public. A facility shall be deemed closed to the public
               when so specified in the hours of operation set forth on a sign posted at the entrance
               thereto, during the hours of darkness when the lights at such facility are turned
               off, when gates or entrances thereto are blocked or locked, when specifically so advised
               by someone employed to supervise, oversee, manage, care for, or protect any such park
               or recreational facility, or when other circumstances would make it obvious to any
               person of reasonable judgment that such facility is closed to the public. (b) The violation of this section shall be a misdemeanor and shall be punishable as provided
               in section 1-7 . (Code 1976, § 22-2; Code 1998, § 58-2)

questions.prompt: In Surfside Beach, when may a bar or beer parlor not sell beer or wine for drinking on site?
choices: Between 2:00 a.m. and 6:00 a.m., Monday through Sunday
Between 11:00 p.m. and 9:00 a.m. on weekdays
questions.answer: Between 2:00 a.m. and 6:00 a.m., Monday through Sunday
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Ord. No. 07-0634, adopted Nov. 13, 2007, added a new Ch. 8, Art. IX, §§ 8-123—8-126,
               pertaining to the regulation of hours establishments may sell or distribute alcoholic
               beverages. For purposes of classification, the editor has redesignated these provisions
               as a new Ch. 2.5, Art. II, §§ 2.5-21—2.5-24.

(a) Between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 6:00 a.m., Monday through Sunday, on the premises
               of any private or nonprofit club, any store, beer parlor, or other place or entity
               of business or establishment authorized by law to sell beer, ale, porter and/or wine
               for the on-premises consumption thereof, it shall be unlawful for: (1) An owner, employee, or person in charge thereof to sell for consumption on premises,
               offer for sale, give away, barter, exchange, or in any manner dispense or permit the
               consumption of any beer, ale, porter and/or wine (as defined in S.C. Code 1976, §
               61-4-10, as amended from time to time, on premises; or (2) Any person to drink or possess in an open container, any beer, ale, porter and/or
               wine on premises of the entity where purchased; or (3) To be open or operate any such club, store, beer parlor, or other such place or entity
               of business or establishment authorized by law to sell beer, ale, porter and/or wine
               for on-premises consumption. (b) The above provisions shall not prohibit during the aforesaid hours the sale or possession
               in sealed containers of beer, ale, porter and/or wine for consumption off the premises. (c) The above provisions shall not prohibit the operation after 2:00 a.m. of an establishment
               bona fide engaged primarily and substantially in the preparation and serving of meals,
               so long as no sale, giveaway, barter, exchange, or other dispensation or consumption
    …

questions.prompt: What form of government did Union choose?
questions.answer: Council form of government
questions.excerpt:
On June 4, 1976, a Certificate of Incorporation was issued to the City of Union by
            the Secretary of State under the powers him enabling. The following is a copy: THE STATE OF SOUTH CAROLINA BY THE SECRETARY OF STATE WHEREAS, the municipality of Union, S. C., is incorporated under the laws of the State
            of South Carolina. AND WHEREAS, a charter has been issued to the above municipality of Union, S. C. (December
            20, 1837). AND WHEREAS, Section 47-20 of the 1962 Code of Laws, as amended, requires that all
            municipalities to adopt a specific form of government. AND WHEREAS, an ordinance was filed with the Secretary of State on June 4, 1976, setting
            forth: FIRST: The name of the municipality is Union, S. C. SECOND: The form of government adopted is Council form of government. NOW THEREFORE, I, O. Frank Thornton, Secretary of State, by virtue of authority vested
            in me by section 47-22 of the 1962 Code, as amended, do hereby issue to the municipality
            of Union, S. C., this Certificate of Incorporation with the privileges, powers and
            immunities, and subject to the limitations prescribed in Act. No. 283 of 1975. Expand (SEAL) GIVEN under my Hand and Seal of the State, this the 4th day of June in the year of
                              our Lord one thousand nine hundred and seventy-six, and in the two hundredth year
                              of the Independence of the United States of America. /s/ O. Frank Thornton Secretary of State
